title: These Alligators Froze Solid in Ice. They're Still Alive

scenes.text: These alligators are frozen in solid ice. And they're alive.
In a North Carolina swamp, the pond froze. The gators felt it coming and pushed their snouts through the surface.
Then they shut down. Heart slows, body goes still, nose stays in the air. It's called brumation.
They can last about a week like that, in water down to 40 degrees.
scenes.keywords: ice surface frozen lake close up

scenes.text: Being cold-blooded, they don't fight the cold. They just wait it out.
The ice melted. Every one of them swam away.

description:
When their swamp froze over, alligators at a North Carolina park pushed their snouts up through the ice and went into brumation, a dormant state where the heart and metabolism slow right down.
They can survive in water as cold as 40 degrees Fahrenheit and hold on for about a week in ice. A video of the frozen gators has been watched more than 11 million times. When the ice thawed, they swam off.
Could you sit still in ice for a week? Comment below.
first_comment: Park staff said the gators were still moving, just extremely slowly. They surface for a breath about once a day in this state. Which animal would you least like to meet in a frozen pond?
